headline: Highest risk is medium: both open-source data-engineering agents have overlapping workflow surfaces, but no documented shared channel or direct evidence of harmful interaction.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between argo-workflows and taipy. A exposes REST API/GRPC and allowlisted egress, while B shows no I/O surfaces or browser use. With no bridge, prompt injection via one agent into the other is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF either agent begins parsing the other's output as instructions, the pathway becomes plausible.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any shared clipboard or message bus.
Review any future parser that consumes peer output.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all inter-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: The profiles do not show a shared workspace, shared OAuth principal, or sensitive data classes flowing from argo-workflows to taipy. A touches artifacts and parameters; B lists no data classes touched and no egress. Without a shared data path, leakage is not supported by the profiles.
conditions: IF both agents are mounted on the same workspace, leakage risk must be re-evaluated.
IF taipy is configured to ingest files from argo-workflows outputs, data leakage becomes plausible.
mitigations: Use separate storage mounts.
Avoid placing secrets in shared artifacts.
Confirm no shared OAuth credentials are used.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls on all workspaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents are data-engineering tools, so overlapping operational intent exists, but the profiles do not show overlapping write surfaces to the same mutable resource. Argo-workflows has API-based orchestration and allowlisted egress; taipy exposes no write or concurrency details. Uncertainty keeps this above none, but below medium.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or git repo, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator gives both agents the same mutable OAuth scope, reassess as medium or higher.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Avoid shared git branches for both agents.
Check for duplicate job names or resource IDs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo-workflows can emit workflow outputs through APIs, and taipy is a data-ops/automation tool that may consume upstream outputs. The profiles do not prove verification between them, so a bad upstream artifact could cascade into downstream actions. Because the interaction is inferred rather than documented, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF taipy consumes argo-workflows outputs without validation, cascading error risk is present.
IF taipy is configured to trigger actions from upstream artifacts, downstream impact increases.
mitigations: Add schema validation on all handoffs.
Require human review for high-impact outputs.
Log and diff upstream artifacts before use.
Use checksum checks on transferred files.
requires-engineering: insert a verification gate between the agents.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either open-source profile. A touches artifacts and parameters; B lists no data classes touched. With no compliance-specific evidence, a breach pathway is not established from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF either deployment processes regulated data such as PHI or EU PII, compliance must be reassessed.
IF one agent is placed under a stricter retention policy than the other for the same data class, mismatch risk appears.
mitigations: Document data classes before deployment.
Keep regulated data out of both agents until reviewed.
Record retention settings for each agent.
requires-engineering: map residency and retention controls per deployment.
